label: 4th original token (p/l/v/s/b/d) after an x/i-initial prefix ending in d/n/h/v
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.0125% of steps). It fires mostly in the original phase (89% of mass), peaking at t=3 (64% of mass) and then t=4. It looks like a higher-order conjunction over the prefix: the first tokens are x/i (first_tok x or i carries 73% of mass), prev2 is in {i,x,n,v}, prev is in {d,n,h,v,r,i}, and the current input is in {p,l,v,1,s,b,2,d}. Top examples: i x d [l], i i d [p], x x d [v], x i v [p]. A small copy-phase component fires on 1 in sequences like h 1 x ... <DEL> h [1]. The precise core predicate (t=3, orig(0) in {x,i}, plus the token sets) has about 84% dev precision but only about 25% recall. Broader versions of the same sets reach about 70% mass recall but only about 2% precision, and trigram/count variants top out near F1 0.2-0.38. So the token preferences are clear, but no single predicate captures the feature. Magnitude is highest for the full x/i x/i d/n/v + p/l/v pattern at t=3. It is essentially silent at t<2 and in late copy steps.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=1 (+5.86), orig0=x (+3.83), orig1=x (+3.65), prev2_tok=<DEL> (+3.62), prev_tok=h (+3.58), prev_tok=n (+3.45). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.24), phase=2 (-2.42), prev3_tok=- (-1.64), orig_idx=-1 (-0.71).
